claim: "That posting bundles three-phase control forms, preparatory meetings, minutes, RFIs, purchase orders and daily production reports into one role ... at $100,000-$140,000." (Section 1; repeated in the founder email: "it lists three-phase control forms, daily reports, RFIs and minutes ... for a $100,000-$140,000 role")
problem: Two different documents are merged into one "posting". The careers page (Quality Control Manager) lists purchase orders, daily Production Reports and RFIs with the PM but shows no salary. The SimplyHired listing (Quality Control Manager/Project Superintendent) carries the $100,000-$140,000 salary, 401(k) match, health, PTO and daily-commute requirement, but lists no purchase orders and does not use the three-phase wording. As written, the salary is attached to duties that appear on a different listing, and the recipient can check their own careers page and not find the number.
fix: Split the sentence: "Your Quality Control Manager posting lists three-phase control, preparatory meetings, minutes, RFIs, purchase orders and daily production reports; a related QC Manager/Project Superintendent listing advertises $100,000-$140,000." Apply the same split in the email draft.

claim: "worked across QCS/RMS plus Word, Excel and Outlook" (Section 1) and "reported across QCS/RMS plus Word and Excel" (email draft)
problem: The careers page asks for "familiarity with QCS/RMS project management software a BIG PLUS" and requires Microsoft Office/Project proficiency. It never says QCS/RMS is the system Benaka's reporting actually runs in. The audit states current practice as fact; it is an inference (a reasonable one, given USACE QC duties, but unlabelled).
fix: Soften to: "...and the posting asks for QCS/RMS familiarity alongside Word, Excel and Outlook." Same wording in the email.

problem: The number is not consistent with the assumptions behind it. The analysis assumes 15-30 hours per bid, 10-20 pursuits a year and a loaded estimator cost of ~$45-55/hour, i.e. 150-600 hours of assembly work in total; $10,000-$30,000 requires 180-670 hours actually removed, which means most or all of the assembly task disappears. The analysis itself only asserts that 15-25% of that time is rework from poor retrieval, which supports roughly $1,000-$8,000. The top of the range is inflated relative to its own basis, and the audit body shows no assumption.
fix: Either restate the range at the supported level (e.g. "$3,000-$10,000 a year in estimator time on the rework share, more if the whole assembly step is drafted") or add the missing assumption inline: "if most compliance-matrix and past-performance assembly time is drafted rather than hand-built."

problem: The body runs to roughly 500 words including headings (about 465 words of prose plus ~35 words of headings), against the ~450-word cap; the "Why this works" block and the Section 3 impact sentence are the main excess.
fix: Cut ~50 words: merge the four "Why this works" bullets into three (fold "Your documents stay yours" into "A person always signs"), and shorten the Section 3 impact sentence to "$6,000-$15,000 a year in clerical time plus avoided penalties - the softest of the three, since the NJ-versus-federal split isn't public."

claim: "Your project history and commendations exist only as flat web pages, so past-performance write-ups start from scratch." (Section 2)
problem: The first half is confirmed (static .html pages in sitemap.xml). "Start from scratch" is an inference about Benaka's internal proposal process with no source, stated as fact.
fix: Frame it: "...so as far as we can tell from outside, past-performance write-ups get rebuilt by hand each time."

claim: "Subs email their details to the general inbox - no form, no portal." (Section 3)
problem: The subcontractors page does say to email details with area of expertise, and there is no vendor portal or prequalification form, so the substance holds. But the contact page tells subcontractors and vendors they may reach the firm "by phone, email, or contact form", so "no form" overstates.
fix: Say "no prequalification form and no vendor portal - just an email address (the general contact form carries no qualification fields)."

claim: "Businesses like yours often find the drafting and reconciling takes the front and back of every day." (Section 1)
problem: An unsourced generalization about the client's peers, presented as an observation. It is the one sentence in the body that asserts something about the industry with no source at all.
fix: Either drop it, or attribute it: "this is the pattern we see across federal general contractors" / "in our experience".

problem: The site says the firm was founded in 1994 and that military facilities are its core specialty; it does not say federal work began in 1994. Slight overstatement, though very likely true.
fix: "You have been building since 1994, mostly for federal clients..." or "founded in 1994 and federal-first ever since..."
